why: `enables` is real, `note` is real, and `concept -enables-> note` is not: the class declares that relationship toward `concept`. Targets are closed WHERE THE CLASS NAMED ONE, which is the one place a hop can be refused on a corpus that did not write `edge_policy: exhaustive` — and it is the case that separates a server typechecking the edge from one checking only that the name exists. The code is `unlicensed-hop`. This contract froze `unlicensed-edge` and `edge-target-class` until 0.15.0 and neither is a rejection code: both are `yidam lint` check ids, reported about a corpus file rather than about a step, and one string cannot mean both. `edge-target-class` in particular was not a near miss — no query path has ever reached it, because this is the rejection a mistargeted hop gets.
